rationale: Wrote the deterministic prefix the @joint_apply_order discriminator asked for and it resolves the apply-side ordering cleanly. The new case builds one voter with newTestRaft over withPeers(1,2,3) and drives the target's own applyConfChange: a JointImplicit learner-add leaves the tracker joint (voters still [1,2,3]) with AutoLeave true; applying a second joint-entering change while joint panics with exactly 'config is already joint'; applying the leave-joint change (an empty ConfChangeV2) makes the tracker non-joint; and the same joint-entering change is then accepted, ending with learners [4,5] and no panic. That confirms the contract's ordering requirement at the apply side and shows the panic is a property of the change/state pair rather than of the harness: any party that applies a joint-entering change while its tracker is joint is rejected, and the way out is to apply the leave-joint entry that precedes it, which is what the leader's own appliedTo path proposes. Draft-side only for now, so the experiment below requests isolated execution of these bytes.

scope.description: Adds a deterministic case (TestAssuranceJointChangeApplyOrder) to the fixed harness: one voter built with newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) is driven through the target's own applyConfChange - a JointImplicit learner-add, then a second joint-entering change while joint (recovered so the panic is observable as data), then the leave-joint change (empty ConfChangeV2), then the same joint-entering change again - and one CA_EVENT reports whether the tracker was joint after the first change, the AutoLeave flag, the voter set after the first change, the recovered panic text for the second change, whether the tracker was still joint after the leave, the recovered panic text for the third change, and the final voter and learner sets. Probes A-C and the sweep are unchanged.
assumptions: The prefix uses only the snapshot's own facilities (newTestRaft, newTestMemoryStorage, withPeers, applyConfChange, ConfChangeV2); no production logic is modified.
The panic is captured with recover so it is recorded as an observation rather than aborting the run; the recovered text is the target's own error string.
This case documents the apply-side ordering requirement; it does not by itself show that a permitted history forces such a change onto an in-order application.
Both cases run in one process and share the same fixed inputs as the rest of the harness.

experiment.prefix: TestAssuranceJointChangeApplyOrder: r := newTestRaft(1,10,1,newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))); r.applyConfChange(ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit, Changes: [{AddLearnerNode, 4}]}); record joint/AutoLeave/voters; then in a recover-guarded closure r.applyConfChange(ConfChangeV2{Transition: JointImplicit, Changes: [{AddLearnerNode, 5}]}); then r.applyConfChange(&ConfChangeV2{}) to leave joint and record the joint flag; then the third change in a second recover-guarded closure; finally emit CA_EVENT joint_change_apply_order with all recorded operands plus the final voter and learner sets.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation with a deterministic prefix added (TestAssuranceJointChangeApplyOrder) that reproduces the apply-side ordering the panic depends on; the harness bytes changed, so fresh execution is requested. A draft-side run reported joint_after_first_joint_change=true, auto_leave=true, voters_after_first=[1,2,3], second_joint_change_panic='config is already joint', joint_after_leave=false, third_change_panic='', learners_final=[4,5], which is construction feedback only.
